title: 아침 식탁에서
focus: 1형식(주어+동사)과 2형식(주어+동사+보어: look, feel)

lines.en: Good morning! The birds sing outside.
Yes, and the toast smells good.
You look sleepy today.
I woke up early. I feel tired.
The milk is warm. Drink it slowly.
Thanks, Mom. Now I feel great!

title: 할머니께 카드 보내기
focus: 3형식(목적어 하나)과 4형식(~에게 …을 주다: send her the card)

lines.en: Dad, I made a card for Grandma.
Great! Let's send her the card today.
Can you buy me a stamp?
Sure. I'll also give you an envelope.
Grandma always tells us funny stories.
lines.ko: 할머니는 늘 우리에게 재미있는 이야기를 해 주셔요.

lines.en: She'll love your card.
lines.ko: 할머니가 네 카드를 정말 좋아하실 거야.

key: Let's send her the card today
Can you buy me a stamp?
I'll also give you an envelope

title: 노래 연습하는 저녁
focus: 5형식(주어+동사+목적어+보어: make me happy, keep the door open)

lines.en: Your new song makes me happy.
lines.ko: 네 새 노래는 나를 행복하게 해.

lines.en: Thanks! My friends call me Little Singer.
Please keep the door open. It's hot.
Okay. But the noise makes Dad angry.
lines.ko: 알았어. 그런데 소리가 아빠를 화나게 해.

lines.en: Then sing softly. I want you to practice.
lines.ko: 그럼 조용히 불러. 네가 연습했으면 좋겠어.

lines.en: Okay. I'll keep my voice low.

key: My friends call me Little Singer

title: 어제, 오늘, 내일
focus: 현재(늘 하는 일)·과거(-ed)·미래(will) 시제 구별

lines.en: What did you do yesterday?
I played soccer with my friends.
Do you play soccer every day?
No, I play only on weekends.
What will you do tomorrow?
I will visit Grandpa with Mom.

title: 팬케이크 굽는 아침
focus: 현재진행(am -ing)·과거진행(was -ing)·미래진행(will be -ing)

lines.en: What are you doing now?
I'm making pancakes for everyone.
Wow! I was sleeping a minute ago.
lines.ko: 와! 나 조금 전까지 자고 있었어.

lines.en: I know. You were snoring loudly!
Haha. What will you be doing after breakfast?
lines.ko: 하하. 아침 먹고 나서 뭐 하고 있을 거야?

lines.en: I'll be playing badminton in the park.

title: 숙제 끝났니?
focus: 현재완료(have p.p.): 완료·경험·계속

lines.en: Have you finished your homework?
Yes, I have just finished it.
Good. Have you ever been to the new library?
lines.ko: 잘했다. 새 도서관에 가 본 적 있니?

lines.en: No, I've never been there.
lines.ko: 아니요, 한 번도 안 가 봤어요.

lines.en: Let's go this Saturday. I've heard it's nice.
Great! I've wanted a new book for weeks.
lines.ko: 좋아요! 몇 주째 새 책이 갖고 싶었거든요.

key: I've wanted a new book for weeks

title: 공원에 가도 돼요?
focus: can/may로 허락 구하기와 가능성 말하기

lines.en: Mom, can I go to the park after lunch?
lines.ko: 엄마, 점심 먹고 공원 가도 돼요?

lines.en: Yes, you can. But it may rain later.
lines.ko: 그래, 가도 돼. 그런데 나중에 비가 올지도 몰라.

lines.en: Can you lend me your umbrella?
Sure. You can take the yellow one.
May I take a snack, too?
Of course you may. Have fun!

key: can I go to the park
May I take a snack, too?

title: 경기 전날 밤
focus: should(~하는 게 좋다)와 have to(~해야 한다)로 의무 말하기

lines.en: I have to wake up early tomorrow.
Why? Do you have a game?
Yes. We have to be at school by seven.
Then you should go to bed now.
Should I eat something before the game?
lines.ko: 경기 전에 뭐 좀 먹어야 할까?

lines.en: Yes, you should eat a banana.
lines.ko: 응, 바나나 하나 먹는 게 좋아.

key: I have to wake up early tomorrow
you should go to bed now

title: 아빠는 어디 가셨지?
focus: may(~일지도 모른다)와 must(~임에 틀림없다)로 추측하기

lines.en: Where is Dad? His shoes are gone.
He may be at the market.
His bike is gone, too.
Then he must be at the park. He loves cycling.
lines.ko: 그럼 공원에 계신 게 틀림없어. 자전거 타는 걸 좋아하시잖아.

lines.en: Look! There's a note on the table.
"Back soon. Buying bread." He must be hungry!
lines.ko: "곧 올게. 빵 사러 감." 배가 고프신 게 분명해!

lines.en: He may bring us some donuts, too.

key: He may be at the market
he must be at the park

title: 등교 준비 시간
focus: 뜻에 주의할 조동사: used to, don't have to, must not, had better

lines.en: I used to hate carrots.
Really? Now you eat them every day.
You don't have to finish your salad.
Thanks. But I must not waste food.
lines.ko: 고마워. 그래도 음식을 낭비하면 안 돼.

lines.en: Good. You'd better hurry, though. The bus is coming.
lines.ko: 좋아. 그래도 서두르는 게 좋겠어. 버스 온다.

lines.en: Oh no! I'd better run now.

key: You don't have to finish your salad

title: 주말 계획 세우기
focus: to부정사의 명사적 용법(~하는 것: want to, It's fun to, My plan is to)

lines.en: What do you want to do this weekend?
I want to learn to swim.
Good idea! It's fun to swim in summer.
lines.ko: 좋은 생각이야! 여름엔 수영하는 게 재밌지.

lines.en: My plan is to go to the pool on Saturday.
lines.ko: 내 계획은 토요일에 수영장에 가는 거야.

lines.en: I hope to join you.
Great! Let's decide what to bring.

key: I want to learn to swim
It's fun to swim in summer
My plan is to go to the pool

title: 배고픈 오후
focus: to부정사의 형용사적 용법(~할: something to drink)

lines.en: I'm so hungry. Is there anything to eat?
There's some bread to share.
Great. I also need something to drink.
Here's some juice. Do you have homework to do?
Yes, I have a lot of math problems to solve.
lines.ko: 응, 풀어야 할 수학 문제가 많아.

lines.en: Then it's time to start!

title: 해돋이 보던 날
focus: to부정사의 부사적 용법(~하려고, ~해서)

lines.en: Why did you get up so early?
I got up early to watch the sunrise.
Wow. Did you see it?
Yes! I was happy to see it.
I went to the store to buy eggs.
Great. Let's make omelets to celebrate the morning!

key: I was happy to see it

title: 농구부에 들어가요
focus: to부정사만 목적어로 쓰는 동사: decide, plan, hope, agree, promise, expect

lines.en: I decided to join the basketball club.
Great! Do you plan to practice every day?
Yes. I hope to play in the next game.
Did Mom agree to buy new shoes?
lines.ko: 엄마가 새 운동화 사 주기로 하셨어?

lines.en: Yes, she promised to buy them on Sunday.
I expect to see you score a basket!
lines.ko: 네가 골 넣는 걸 꼭 보고 싶어!

key: I decided to join the basketball club
I hope to play in the next game

title: 무거운 상자 옮기기
focus: 중요 부정사 구문: too ~ to, ~ enough to, It's ~ for 사람 to, seem to

lines.en: This box is too heavy to lift.
lines.ko: 이 상자는 너무 무거워서 못 들겠어.

lines.en: Let me help. I'm strong enough to carry it.
lines.ko: 내가 도와줄게. 나는 이걸 나를 만큼 힘이 세.

lines.en: Thanks. It's hard for me to move it alone.
What's inside? It seems to be books.
Yes, my old comic books.
It will take an hour to read them all!

key: It's hard for me to move it

title: 아침 운동 이야기
focus: 문장 맨 앞에 오는 동명사 주어(~하는 것은)

lines.en: Running in the morning feels great.
lines.ko: 아침에 달리는 건 기분이 정말 좋아.

lines.en: Really? Getting up early is hard for me.
lines.ko: 정말? 나는 일찍 일어나는 게 힘들어.

lines.en: Sleeping late isn't good for you.
lines.ko: 늦잠 자는 건 몸에 안 좋아.

lines.en: I know. But reading at night is my favorite thing.
lines.ko: 알아. 그런데 밤에 책 읽는 게 제일 좋은걸.

lines.en: Then let's try walking together after school.
lines.ko: 그럼 방과 후에 같이 걸어 보자.

lines.en: Okay! Walking with you sounds fun.

key: Running in the morning feels great
Getting up early is hard for me

title: 방 청소하는 토요일
focus: 동명사만 목적어로 쓰는 동사: finish, keep, mind, stop, enjoy

lines.en: Have you finished cleaning your room?
Almost. I keep finding old toys.
Do you mind giving some to your cousin?
Not at all. I've stopped playing with them.
Thanks. You enjoy helping others, don't you?
lines.ko: 고마워. 너는 남 돕는 걸 좋아하는구나?

lines.en: Yes! Now I'll finish putting them in a box.

key: Have you finished cleaning your room?
Do you mind giving some to your cousin?

title: 라켓을 깜빡했어
focus: 동명사와 to부정사 비교: remember/forget/stop/try + -ing vs to

lines.en: Did you remember to bring your racket?
Oh no! I forgot to bring it.
It's okay. Try using my old one.
lines.ko: 괜찮아. 내 옛날 라켓을 한번 써 봐.

lines.en: Thanks. I remember playing with it last year.
lines.ko: 고마워. 작년에 그걸로 쳤던 기억이 나.

lines.en: Let's stop talking and start the game.
Wait! Let me stop to tie my shoes.
lines.ko: 잠깐! 신발 끈 좀 묶고 갈게.

key: Did you remember to bring your racket?
I remember playing with it last year

title: 영화 보고 온 날
focus: 감정 분사: -ing(~하게 하는) vs -ed(~하게 된, 느끼는)

lines.en: How was the movie?
It was exciting! I was so excited.
Mine was boring. I got bored and slept.
Haha! Our ending was really surprising.
lines.ko: 하하! 우리 영화는 결말이 정말 놀라웠어.

lines.en: Were you surprised, too?
Yes! I was so surprised I screamed.

title: 길에서 만난 강아지
focus: 분사구문으로 두 문장 연결하기(~하다가, ~해서)

lines.en: Walking home, I saw a cute puppy.
Really? Where was it?
Near the park. Seeing me, it wagged its tail.
lines.ko: 공원 근처에. 나를 보더니 꼬리를 흔들었어.

lines.en: So cute! Did you pet it?
Yes. Feeling happy, I smiled all the way home.
lines.ko: 응. 기분이 좋아서 집까지 계속 웃었어.

lines.en: Finishing breakfast, we can go see it together!
lines.ko: 아침 다 먹고 같이 보러 가자!

key: Walking home, I saw a cute puppy
Seeing me, it wagged its tail

title: 우리 집 아침 풍경
focus: 동시 동작 분사(~하면서): sitting ... reading

lines.en: Dad is sitting on the sofa reading the news.
lines.ko: 아빠는 소파에 앉아 뉴스를 읽고 계셔.

lines.en: And Mom is cooking, humming a song.
Look! Our cat is lying there, watching the birds.
lines.ko: 봐! 고양이가 누워서 새들을 구경하고 있어.

lines.en: Haha. I'm eating toast, listening to music.
lines.ko: 하하. 나는 음악 들으면서 토스트 먹고 있어.

lines.en: Don't run to school eating toast!
Okay. I'll finish it sitting here.

key: sitting on the sofa reading the news

title: 목마른 아침
focus: 상태는 be동사(Are you ~? / I'm not), 행동은 do동사(Do you ~? / we don't)

lines.en: Are you hungry?
No, I'm not. But I'm thirsty.
Do you want some orange juice?
Yes, please. Do we have any ice?
No, we don't. Is cold water okay?
Yes, it is. Thanks, Mom!

key: Do you want some orange juice?

title: 설거지 당번
focus: 사역동사: make(억지로 시키다), let(허락하다), have(맡겨서 ~되게 하다)

lines.en: Why are you washing the dishes?
Mom made me wash them. I broke a cup.
Oh no. Let me help you.
Thanks. Will Dad let us ride bikes later?
lines.ko: 고마워. 이따 아빠가 자전거 타게 해 주실까?

lines.en: Yes. I had my bike fixed yesterday.
lines.ko: 응. 어제 내 자전거 수리 맡겨서 고쳤어.

lines.en: Great! Let's finish quickly then.

title: 정원의 할아버지
focus: 지각동사 see, hear, feel + 목적어 + 동사원형/-ing

lines.en: Did you hear someone singing?
Yes! I heard Grandpa sing in the garden.
lines.ko: 응! 할아버지가 정원에서 노래하시는 걸 들었어.

lines.en: I saw him water the flowers, too.
He looks so happy.
I can feel the warm wind blowing.
Let's go out and watch him work.

key: I saw him water the flowers

title: 엄마 생일 파티
focus: 수동태(be + p.p. + by)와 능동태 구조 비교

lines.en: Wow, this cake is delicious! Who made it?
It was made by Dad.
And these flowers?
They were bought by your sister.
The table was set by me!
Great teamwork! Dad baked the cake, and everyone helped.
lines.ko: 팀워크 최고! 아빠는 케이크를 굽고 다 같이 도왔네.

key: They were bought by your sister
The table was set by me

title: 오늘의 집안일
focus: 조동사가 있는 수동태: should be p.p., will be p.p.

lines.en: The trash should be taken out today.
Okay, I'll do it after breakfast.
And the plants should be watered, too.
Sure. When will the new sofa be delivered?
It will be delivered this afternoon.
Then the living room should be cleaned first!

key: will the new sofa be delivered
It will be delivered this afternoon

title: 사라진 셔츠
focus: 수동태로 쓸 수 없는 동사: happen, fit, resemble, disappear, appear

lines.en: What happened to your shirt?
Nothing happened. It just doesn't fit me.
lines.ko: 아무 일도 없었어. 그냥 나한테 안 맞아.

lines.en: You resemble Dad in that shirt!
Haha. Actually, it's his old shirt.
Where did your shirt go?
It disappeared after the trip.
It will appear someday, I'm sure.

title: 날개가 있다면
focus: 가정법 과거(If + 과거, would/could + 동사원형): 지금 사실과 반대 상상

lines.en: If I had wings, I would fly to school.
If I were you, I would fly to the beach!
Haha. If it were Saturday, we could go together.
lines.ko: 하하. 토요일이라면 같이 갈 수 있을 텐데.

lines.en: If I had more time, I would sleep more.
lines.ko: 시간이 더 있다면 잠을 더 잘 텐데.

lines.en: Me too. But now we have to hurry.
Okay, let's go!

key: If I had wings, I would fly to school

title: 버스를 놓친 아침
focus: 가정법 과거완료(If + had p.p., would have p.p.): 지난 일 후회

lines.en: We missed the bus this morning.
If we had woken up earlier, we would have caught it.
lines.ko: 더 일찍 일어났다면 탈 수 있었을 텐데.

lines.en: I know. If I hadn't played games, I would have slept earlier.
lines.ko: 맞아. 게임을 안 했다면 더 일찍 잤을 텐데.

lines.en: And Mom would have driven us if she had been home.
lines.ko: 엄마가 집에 계셨다면 태워 주셨을 텐데.

lines.en: Tonight, let's go to bed early.
Deal. No games after nine!

title: 강아지 키우고 싶어
focus: I wish + 과거(~라면 좋겠다)와 What if ~?(~하면 어떨까/어쩌지)

lines.en: I wish I had a puppy.
Me too. I wish we lived in a bigger house.
lines.ko: 나도. 더 큰 집에 살면 좋겠어.

lines.en: What if we asked Mom and Dad?
What if they say no?
Then I wish I could visit Grandma's dog every week.
lines.ko: 그럼 할머니네 강아지를 매주 보러 갈 수 있으면 좋겠어.

lines.en: Good idea. Let's ask them at breakfast.
lines.ko: 좋은 생각이야. 아침 먹을 때 여쭤보자.

key: I wish I had a puppy
What if we asked Mom and Dad?

title: 장보기 목록 만들기
focus: 단수(a/one + 명사)와 복수(two + 명사-s)

lines.en: How many apples do we have?
We have one apple and three bananas.
lines.ko: 사과 한 개랑 바나나 세 개 있어.

lines.en: I need two eggs for the pancakes.
There is only one egg in the box.
Then I'll buy some eggs and a bottle of milk.
lines.ko: 그럼 달걀이랑 우유 한 병 사 올게.

lines.en: Please get two boxes of strawberries, too!

title: 농장 가는 날
focus: 불규칙 복수형: teeth, feet, sheep, geese, fish, children

lines.en: Children, did you brush your teeth?
Yes! And I washed my feet, too.
Good. Today we're going to the farm.
Will we see sheep and geese?
Yes, and lots of fish in the pond.
Yay! I'll bring two boxes of snacks.

title: 간식 시간
focus: 셀 수 없는 명사 세기: a glass of, two slices of, a piece of

lines.en: Can I have some water, please?
Sure. Do you want a glass of milk, too?
No, thanks. Is there any bread?
There are two slices of bread and some cheese.
lines.ko: 빵 두 조각이랑 치즈가 좀 있어.

lines.en: Great. I'll also have an apple.
Here's a piece of cake for later.
lines.ko: 이따 먹을 케이크 한 조각도 여기 있어.

title: 가족과 팀의 주말
focus: 집합명사: family, team, audience, people, class

lines.en: My family is going camping this weekend.
lines.ko: 우리 가족은 이번 주말에 캠핑 가.

lines.en: Sounds fun! My team has a soccer game.
lines.ko: 재밌겠다! 우리 팀은 축구 경기가 있어.

lines.en: Is your team strong this year?
Yes! And the audience is always loud.
lines.ko: 응! 그리고 관중이 항상 엄청 시끄러워.

lines.en: Many people come to watch, right?
Yes. Our whole class comes to cheer!
lines.ko: 응. 우리 반 전체가 응원하러 와!

key: My team has a soccer game

title: 강아지 좋아해?
focus: dogs(그 종류 전체) vs a dog(한 마리) vs the dog(바로 그 개)

lines.en: I like dogs. Do you?
Yes! I want a dog for my birthday.
lines.ko: 응! 생일 선물로 강아지 한 마리 갖고 싶어.

lines.en: Look! The dog next door is barking.
The dog is so cute. Cats are cute, too.
lines.ko: 그 개 정말 귀엽다. 고양이도 귀엽고.

lines.en: Do you have a cat?
No, but the cats at Grandma's house love me.
lines.ko: 아니, 그래도 할머니 댁 고양이들이 날 좋아해.

key: The dog next door is barking

title: 마당의 고양이
focus: a(처음 말할 때) vs the(이미 아는 것, 하나뿐인 것)

lines.en: I saw a cat in the yard.
Was the cat black or white?
Black. It was sleeping under a tree.
Is that the tree near the gate?
Yes! Let's give the cat some water.
lines.ko: 응! 그 고양이한테 물 좀 주자.

lines.en: Good idea. Bring a bowl from the kitchen.
lines.ko: 좋은 생각이야. 부엌에서 그릇 하나 가져와.

key: I saw a cat in the yard
Was the cat black or white?
Is that the tree near the gate?

title: 피아노 연습
focus: 유용한 관사 용법: a = ~마다(twice a week), play the + 악기, the sun/moon

lines.en: How often do you take piano lessons?
Twice a week. I love playing the piano.
lines.ko: 일주일에 두 번. 피아노 치는 거 정말 좋아해.

lines.en: Me too. I practice an hour a day.
lines.ko: 나도. 나는 하루에 한 시간 연습해.

lines.en: Wow! Look, the moon is still in the sky.
lines.ko: 와! 봐, 달이 아직 하늘에 떠 있어.

lines.en: And the sun is rising. Beautiful!
Let's play the guitar together tonight.

title: 학교 가기 전
focus: 관사 없이 쓰는 표현: have breakfast, go to school, by bus, go to bed

lines.en: Did you have breakfast?
Yes. Now I'm ready to go to school.
lines.ko: 네. 이제 학교 갈 준비 됐어요.

lines.en: Are you going by bus today?
No, I'm going on foot. It's sunny.
Come home early. We'll have dinner at six.
Okay! And I'll go to bed early tonight.

title: 좋아하는 과목과 운동
focus: 운동(play soccer)과 과목(science, math) 앞에는 관사를 쓰지 않음

lines.en: What's your favorite subject?
I like science and math.
Cool. Do you play soccer after school?
No, I play basketball on Mondays.
I play tennis with Dad on Sundays.
Let's play badminton together this weekend!

title: 팬케이크 재료 확인
focus: many(셀 수 있는 명사) vs much(셀 수 없는 명사)

lines.en: How much milk do we have?
Not much. Just one glass.
How many eggs are there?
There are many eggs. About ten.
Good. Don't put too much sugar in the pancakes.
lines.ko: 좋아. 팬케이크에 설탕 너무 많이 넣지 마.

lines.en: Okay. But many kids love sweet pancakes!
lines.ko: 알았어. 그래도 아이들은 달콤한 팬케이크를 좋아하는걸!

key: How much milk do we have?

title: 과학 과제 도와줘
focus: a few(셀 수 있는 것 조금) vs a little(셀 수 없는 것 조금), little(거의 없는)

lines.en: Do you have a few minutes?
Sure. What's up?
I need a little help with my science project.
Okay. I have a few ideas.
lines.ko: 좋아. 나한테 아이디어가 몇 개 있어.

lines.en: Thanks! I have little time before Friday.
Don't worry. Just add a little color to the poster.
lines.ko: 걱정 마. 포스터에 색만 조금 더 넣어 봐.

title: 학교 소풍
focus: all(모두) / some(몇몇, 약간) / no(하나도 없는)

lines.en: Did all the students come to the picnic?
Yes, all of them came.
Great! Did they bring some food?
Some brought sandwiches, and some brought fruit.
lines.ko: 몇 명은 샌드위치를, 몇 명은 과일을 가져왔어.

lines.en: What about drinks?
No one brought juice! There's no juice at all.
lines.ko: 아무도 주스를 안 가져왔어! 주스가 하나도 없어.

title: 채소 다 먹었니?
focus: all(전부) / almost(거의) / most(대부분) 구별

lines.en: Did you eat all your vegetables?
Almost. I ate most of them.
Most kids don't like carrots.
I almost finished the carrots, too!
Good job! Your plate is almost empty.
Yes! All my friends eat vegetables now.
lines.ko: 네! 이제 제 친구들은 다 채소를 먹어요.

title: 이거 누구 가방이야?
focus: 인칭대명사: mine, him, his, theirs, them

lines.en: Is this your bag?
No, it isn't mine. It's my brother's.
lines.ko: 아니, 내 거 아니야. 우리 형 거야.

lines.en: Where is he? I'll give it to him.
He's in his room with his friends.
Are these shoes theirs?
Yes. They left them by the door.

title: 경기 날 아침
focus: 의문대명사: who(누구), what(무엇), which(어느 것), whose(누구의 것)

lines.en: Who called you this morning?
My coach. We have a game today.
What time does it start?
At two. Which jersey should I wear?
The blue one. Whose socks are these?
lines.ko: 파란 거. 이 양말은 누구 거야?

lines.en: They're mine! Thanks.

title: 내 방 구경
focus: 지시대명사: this/these(가까운 것), that/those(먼 것)

lines.en: Is this your new pencil case?
Yes, and these are my new pens.
lines.ko: 응, 그리고 이건 내 새 펜들이야.

lines.en: Nice! What's that on the shelf?
That's my soccer trophy.
And those boxes?
Those are gifts for Mom's birthday. Shh!

key: Is this your new pencil case?

title: 쿠키 두 개
focus: 부정대명사: one(하나), the other(나머지 하나), another(하나 더), the others

lines.en: I have two cookies. One is chocolate.
lines.ko: 쿠키가 두 개 있어. 하나는 초코야.

lines.en: What about the other?
The other is strawberry. Which one do you want?
lines.ko: 나머지 하나는 딸기야. 어느 거 먹을래?

lines.en: The chocolate one, please. Can I have another?
lines.ko: 초코 거 줘. 하나 더 먹어도 돼?

lines.en: Sorry, but I can bake another one later.
lines.ko: 미안, 대신 이따 하나 더 구워 줄게.

lines.en: Thanks! I'll share it with the others.

title: 텅 빈 냉장고
focus: 부정대명사: anyone, everyone, anything, nothing, something, both

lines.en: Is anyone home?
Yes, I'm here. Everyone else went out.
lines.ko: 응, 나 여기 있어. 다른 사람들은 다 나갔어.

lines.en: Is there anything to eat?
There's nothing in the fridge, sorry.
Then let's make something together.
Both of us like noodles. Let's cook those!
lines.ko: 우리 둘 다 국수 좋아하잖아. 그거 끓이자!

title: 시험 보는 날 아침
focus: 기분·상태를 나타내는 형용사: tired, nervous, calm, full, happy

lines.en: You look tired this morning.
I am. I was nervous about my test.
Don't worry. You studied hard.
Thanks. Now I feel calm.
Eat this. You will feel full and happy.
lines.ko: 이거 먹어. 배부르고 기분 좋아질 거야.

lines.en: Mmm, it's delicious. I'm ready now!

key: I was nervous about my test

title: 그림 잘 그리는 친구
focus: 형용사 + 전치사: good at, interested in, afraid of, proud of, full of

lines.en: You're good at drawing!
Thanks. I'm interested in animals.
This lion looks real. Are you afraid of lions?
lines.ko: 이 사자 진짜 같다. 너 사자 무서워?

lines.en: A little! But I'm proud of this picture.
Your notebook is full of animals.
Yes. I'm famous for it in my class!

title: 달리기 연습 후
focus: 같은 단어 다른 뜻 형용사: present(출석한/현재의), right(오른쪽/옳은), fine(괜찮은/멋진)

lines.en: Was everyone present at practice today?
Yes. Minho was late, but he came.
How is your right leg?
It's fine. You were right about stretching.
Good. What's your present goal?
To run a fine race on Saturday!

key: Was everyone present at practice today?

title: 경기 응원 온 가족
focus: 형용사 + that절: glad that, sure that, afraid that, sorry that

lines.en: I'm glad that you came to my game.
I'm sure that you'll win today.
I'm afraid that I'll make a mistake.
Don't worry. I'm happy that you're trying.
lines.ko: 걱정 마. 네가 도전하는 것만으로도 기뻐.

lines.en: Thanks. I'm sorry that I was late.
It's okay. Go and have fun!

key: I'm afraid that I'll make a mistake

title: 운동회 다음 날
focus: 부사의 역할: 동사·형용사·다른 부사·문장 전체를 꾸밈

lines.en: You ran really fast today!
Thanks. I practiced very hard.
Luckily, the weather was perfect.
Yes. The field was very quiet early in the morning.
lines.ko: 응. 이른 아침엔 운동장이 아주 조용했어.

lines.en: Please speak quietly. The baby is sleeping.
Oops! Sorry. I'll talk softly.

title: 늦잠 잔 아침
focus: 뜻이 다른 부사 짝: hard(열심히)/hardly(거의 ~않다), late/lately, near/nearly

lines.en: You studied hard last night.
Yes, but I hardly slept.
Have you been sleeping well lately?
Not really. I went to bed late again.
It's nearly eight! Hurry up.
Oh no! Luckily, the school is near.

key: I went to bed late again

title: 아침밥 습관
focus: 빈도부사(always, usually, sometimes, often)와 부정부사(never, seldom, hardly)

lines.en: Do you always eat breakfast?
Usually. But I sometimes skip it.
I never skip breakfast.
Wow. Do you often eat rice?
Yes. I seldom eat bread in the morning.
lines.ko: 응. 아침에 빵은 좀처럼 안 먹어.

lines.en: I hardly ever eat rice in the morning!
lines.ko: 나는 아침에 밥을 거의 안 먹는데!

title: 저녁 식탁 차리기
focus: too(너무 ~해서 안 되는)와 enough(충분히, 충분한)

lines.en: Is the soup ready?
Yes, but it's too hot to eat now.
lines.ko: 응, 그런데 지금은 너무 뜨거워서 못 먹어.

lines.en: Is there enough bread for everyone?
lines.ko: 다 같이 먹을 만큼 빵이 충분해?

lines.en: Yes, we have enough bread.
This chair is too small for Dad.
Then he can sit here. This one is big enough.
lines.ko: 그럼 여기 앉으시면 돼. 이건 충분히 커.

title: 새 강아지 이야기
focus: ago(지금부터 ~전에)와 before(그 전에, 이전에)

lines.en: When did you get your puppy?
Two months ago.
Had you ever had a pet before?
lines.ko: 그 전에 반려동물 키워 본 적 있어?

lines.en: Yes. I had a fish a long time ago.
I saw your puppy at the park three days ago.
lines.ko: 사흘 전에 공원에서 네 강아지 봤어.

lines.en: Really? He'd never been there before.
lines.ko: 정말? 그 전엔 거기 가 본 적이 없었는데.

key: Had you ever had a pet before?

title: 아빠만큼 컸네
focus: 동등 비교: as + 형용사/부사 + as

lines.en: You are as tall as Dad now!
Really? But I can't run as fast as he can.
lines.ko: 정말요? 그래도 아빠만큼 빨리 달리진 못해요.

lines.en: You eat as much as him, though.
Haha. Your soup is as good as a restaurant's!
lines.ko: 하하. 엄마 수프는 식당 수프만큼 맛있어요!

lines.en: Thank you! Eat as much as you want.
Okay! I'll finish it as quickly as I can.

title: 축구 vs 야구
focus: 비교급: -er than, more ~ than(더 ~한), less ~ than(덜 ~한)

lines.en: Is soccer more fun than baseball?
For me, yes. Soccer is faster than baseball.
But baseball is less tiring than soccer.
That's true. You're a better hitter than me.
lines.ko: 맞아. 너는 나보다 공을 잘 쳐.

lines.en: And you run faster than me.
Let's play both this weekend!

title: 우리 반 최고는?
focus: 최상급: the -est, the most ~, the best

lines.en: Who is the tallest in your class?
Junho is. He's the fastest runner, too.
What's the most popular sport at school?
lines.ko: 학교에서 제일 인기 있는 운동은 뭐야?

lines.en: Dodgeball! It's the best game ever.
And what's the best part of your day?
lines.ko: 그럼 하루 중에 제일 좋은 때는 언제야?

lines.en: Breakfast with you, Mom. It's the happiest time!
lines.ko: 엄마랑 아침 먹을 때요. 제일 행복한 시간이에요!

key: Who is the tallest in your class?
